A pre-broken Maestro BPMN file ships two blocking defects (an exclusive-gateway branch with no condition expression, and a condition expression that references an undeclared variable). 1	# Maestro BPMN Validator (bundled, offline)
2	
3	A dependency-light, offline semantic validator for UiPath Maestro BPMN XML. It
4	parses the BPMN with `bpmn-moddle` using the UiPath extension descriptor (the
5	same `getModdle()` + `fromXML()` pattern as PO.Frontend), reconstructs the
6	PO.Frontend `Node[] / Edge[] / CanvasState` model from the parse tree, and runs
7	**all 19** PO.Frontend validation rules plus the variable-validation checks
8	(`VARIABLE_DOES_NOT_EXIST`, including element-local `result.X`, and the
9	flow-order `VARIABLE_NOT_SET` warning) and an optional connection-liveness ping.
10	
11	> **Authoring scope:** everything under `test/fixtures/` is validator test data,
12	> not authoring material. **Do not read the fixtures to infer the BPMN pattern**
13	> — it is the top reason authoring runs out of time. Author from the complete
14	> minimal file in
15	> [../references/structural-bpmn.md](../references/structural-bpmn.md#a-complete-minimal-file-author-from-this-not-from-fixtures)
16	> instead. This README documents the validator and its test suite; run the
17	> validator (below) as your check, and leave the corpus to CI.
18	
19	## Usage
20	
21	```bash
22	npm install
23	node validate-bpmn.mjs <bpmn-file> [resources]
24	```
25	
26	- Prints `VALID` and exits `0` when there are no ERROR-severity findings.
27	- Otherwise lists every finding (rule code + message) and exits `1`.
28	- WARNING-severity findings are printed but do not gate.
29	- A strict XML well-formedness gate (sax strict mode) runs **before** the
30	  `bpmn-moddle` parse and exits `2` on malformed input — unescaped `&`/`<`, `--`
31	  inside a comment, mismatched tags. `bpmn-moddle`'s SAX parser is lenient and
32	  would accept these, but the Studio Web canvas import rejects them, so the
33	  validator must too: a safety net that is more permissive than the real import
34	  gives false confidence.
35	- `resources` (optional): a numeric folder id (or comma-separated release names)
36	  for the connection-liveness ping via the `uip` CLI. Best-effort; a missing or
37	  unauthenticated CLI is reported as a NOTE, never a hard failure.
38	
39	```bash
40	npm test   # runs all three suites below; green = no drift from the frontend
41	```
42	
43	## Test suites (`test/`)
44	
45	`npm test` runs the layers below and asserts all 29 rule codes are exercised
46	(plus a CLI well-formedness-gate check):
47	
48	1. **Crafted-invalid XML coverage** (`run-tests.mjs`): for each rule, a minimal
49	   BPMN that should trip exactly that rule's code, plus a check that valid twins
50	   don't. Proves the full parse → model → rules pipeline end-to-end.
51	2. **Ported PO.Frontend rule tests** (`test/ported-rule-tests.mjs`): a 1:1
52	   translation of every `PO.Frontend/src/services/validation/bpmn/rules/*.test.ts`
53	   case plus the variable-validation cases from `VariableUtil.test.ts`
54	   (173 assertions). Each case carries a `// FE:` comment naming the
55	   originating frontend test and runs the same synthetic Node/Edge/CanvasState
56	   graph through **our** rule engine. This is the primary drift detector: if our
57	   port disagrees with a frontend test's expectation, this suite fails.
58	3. **Integration over real `.bpmn` files** (`test/integration.test.mjs`): every
59	   file in `test/fixtures/` is a real, externally-validated artifact (backend
60	   BpmnParser/Worker/Athena/V2-E2E TestData, and PO.Frontend editor mocks),
61	   bundled so the suite is self-contained in CI. These files exist to exercise
62	   the rule engine — they are **not** authoring templates; see the authoring-scope
63	   note at the top before reaching for one as an example. `fixtures/known-good/`
64	   must produce **zero** ERROR-severity findings; `fixtures/expected-findings/` assert
65	   the exact ERROR codes the frontend would also raise (each verified by reading
66	   the file). Set `MAESTRO_BPMN_TESTDATA` / `MAESTRO_BPMN_FRONTEND_MOCKS` to also
67	   sweep a live corpus during development.
68	
69	## Parity status
70	
71	**Full parity with the PO.Frontend rule engine is now reached for every rule
72	except two clearly-bounded residuals (below).** Each rule is a faithful port of
73	the frontend rule of the same name: same inputs → same outputs, verified by the
74	1:1 ported test suite (frontend test inputs) and the real-`.bpmn` integration
75	corpus (zero ERROR findings on 31 known-good files; exact ERROR-code match on 28
76	expected-findings files).
77	
78	### Closed gaps (now at parity)
79	
80	1. **`RequiredFields` flags ABSENT required fields, not only present-but-empty.**
81	   Frontend `RequiredFieldsRule.ts:24-27` + `ValidateRequiredFieldsInData.ts:15-16`
82	   fire on `field.required && isNilOrEmpty(field.value)`. On canvas every field a
83	   serviceType declares is present in node data, so an *unbound* required field is
84	   present-with-empty-value. In exported BPMN that field is simply absent. The
85	   model (`model.mjs`) attaches the serviceType's full registry required-field name
86	   set (`bpmn-spec.json`, 128 `required` entries) as `uipath.requiredFieldNames`,
87	   and the rule now treats an absent required name exactly as the frontend treats
88	   an unbound field. Present-but-empty still fires too, in the frontend's
89	   context → inputs → outputs order, one finding per node.
90	2. **`VARIABLE_NOT_SET` (WARNING) is now implemented.** Port of the flow-order
91	   reachability half of `VariableUtil.validateVariablesInExpression`
92	   (`VariableUtil.ts:758-866`), built on the pure topology helpers
93	   `getSourceEdgeMappings` (`:121-130`), `mapNodeOutputsToVariables` (`:539-579`),
94	   `getVariablesForSubProcess` (`:495-525`), `getAvailableVariablesFromSourceNodes`
95	   (`:303-389`, backward BFS over sequence-flow edges + boundary re-parenting +
96	   subprocess scope), and `getAvailableVariablesForElement` (`:401-481`, parent
97	   chain + event-subprocess shared scope + subprocess EndEvent exposure). A
98	   *declared* variable referenced where no flow path reaches its producer fires
99	   `VARIABLE_NOT_SET` (WARNING, non-gating). **Skipped entirely for Case
100	   Management** (`VariableUtil.ts:826-828`). Root variables are globally available
101	   and never warn.
102	3. **`result.X` existence is now validated element-locally.** Frontend puts an
103	   unresolved `result.X` in the non-existing set (`VariableUtil.ts:263`) and a
104	   `result.X` is valid only if `X` names one of the *referencing element's own*
105	   outputs (`isResultVariableValidForElement`, `:166-178`). The port previously
106	   skipped all `result.` refs unconditionally; it now resolves `result.X` against
107	   the element's own output identifiers and fires `VARIABLE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` for an
108	   invalid one (edge conditions have no own outputs, so every `result.X` on an
109	   edge is invalid, matching the frontend).
110	4. **`ConnectionRule` unknown-type fallback now returns `false`.** Frontend
111	   `canNodeTypesBeConnected` (`BPMNTypesUtils.ts:51-82`) returns **false** when no
112	   rule matches the source type, yielding `INVALID_CONNECTION_TYPE` (WARNING). The
113	   port previously returned `true` for unknown source types; it now matches the
114	   frontend. The abstract-type inheritance the frontend additionally walks is
115	   already folded into our concrete allow-map (every concrete activity/event type
116	   has an explicit entry), so an unknown source type genuinely has no rule. The
117	   ported `ConnectionRule` test was un-doctored to the frontend's actual input
118	   (source `"output"` → target `"input"`, both unknown) per `ConnectionRule.test.ts:33-43`.
119	5. **Custom-output accessor gating aligned to the frontend.** Both the existence
120	   check and `VARIABLE_NOT_SET` now collect a custom output's `source` only when
121	   `getAccessorFromType(type) === "source"`, and `body` only when the accessor is
122	   `body` (`VariableUtil.ts:952-968`).
123	
124	### Earlier fixes (already at parity before this round)
125	
126	6. **Empty `<conditionExpression/>` crash — FIXED.** An empty condition element
127	   parses to a moddle object with no `.body`; the model now treats it as "no
128	   condition" (frontend behavior) instead of crashing the string-based rules.
129	7. **`FakeJoinRule` over-firing — FIXED (match frontend behavior).** See the
130	   residual note below.
131	8. **`validateRequiredFields(null)` crash — FIXED.** Matches the frontend's
132	   `if (!nodes || !edges) return []` guard.
133	9. **`VARIABLE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` false positives on node-output variables — FIXED.**
134	   A node's `<uipath:output var="x">` declares variable `x`
135	   (`mapNodeOutputsToVariables`: `id: v.var`); these are now in the known-id set,
136	   and script-task IO under `uipath:Mapping` is recognized.
137	
138	## Genuine residuals (the only two)
139	
140	These are the **only** places this port is not byte-for-byte identical to the
141	frontend, and both are bounded and justified — not drift.
142	
143	- **Dynamic IS-connector required-ness needs `registry get` enrichment (shared
144	  with the frontend).** For Integration-Service connector activity types whose
145	  required fields are NOT in the static `bpmn-spec.json` registry — their
146	  required-ness only materializes after a live `registry get` enrichment — the
147	  model has no `requiredFieldNames`, so `RequiredFields` stays conservative
148	  (only present-but-empty fires; absence cannot be judged). **The frontend has
149	  the identical limitation:** it also needs that enrichment to learn the field is
150	  required. For every serviceType present in the static registry, absent-required
151	  detection is at full parity.
152	- **`FAKE_JOIN` is dormant on real/exported BPMN (faithful to the frontend).**
153	  The frontend `FakeJoinRule` matches only the **literal** abstract types
154	  `"bpmn:Activity"` / `"bpmn:Event"`, but the canvas assigns every node its
155	  **concrete** `$type` (`bpmn:Task`, `bpmn:EndEvent`, …; `bpmn-from-xml.ts` sets
156	  `type: $type`). The rule therefore never fires on exported BPMN — its own
157	  source carries a `TODO` admitting it must be rewritten to walk the inherited-
158	  type chain, which it does not yet do. The port applies the frontend's exact
159	  predicate, so it is faithful (same inputs → same outputs); its logic is proven
160	  in the ported suite (which feeds literal abstract types, like the frontend
161	  test) and is intentionally not triggerable via real XML.
162	
163	## Architecture (Phase 1 → Phase 2)
164	
165	| File | Role |
166	| --- | --- |
167	| `rules.mjs` | **Self-contained rule engine** — the swap target. In Phase 2 this single module is replaced by the published npm package with no behavior change. |
168	| `model.mjs` | Integration glue: reconstructs the frontend model from the moddle tree; bundles registry metadata. |
169	| `validate-bpmn.mjs` | CLI entry: parse → build model → run rules → gate. |
170	| `bpmn-spec.json` | Bundled maestro-sdk registry, consumed offline for RequiredFields. |
171	| `uipath-moddle.v1.json` | Verbatim UiPath moddle descriptor from PO.Frontend. |
172

202	## RequiredFields parity note
203	
204	The PO.Frontend `RequiredFields` rule fires when `field.required && isNilOrEmpty(field.value)`
205	(`ValidateRequiredFieldsInData.ts:15-16`). On the canvas every field a serviceType
206	declares is present in node data with its `required` flag, so an *unbound*
207	required field is present-with-empty-value and is flagged.
208	
209	Offline, `field.required` is recovered from the bundled registry
210	(`bpmn-spec.json`, 128 `required` entries keyed by serviceType; names are the
211	serialized names) and the model attaches the full required-name set as
212	`uipath.requiredFieldNames`. The rule fires for a required field that is either
213	**present-but-empty** OR entirely **absent** from the serialized data (an absent
214	required field is the exported-BPMN form of the canvas's unbound field), in the
215	frontend's context → inputs → outputs order, one finding per node. This reaches
216	full parity for every serviceType present in the static registry.
217	
218	The single bounded exception is dynamic Integration-Service connector activity
219	types whose required-ness is **not** in the static registry (it only
220	materializes after a live `registry get` enrichment): for those,
221	`requiredFieldNames` is undefined and absence cannot be judged, so the rule stays
222	conservative (only present-but-empty fires). The frontend shares this exact
